title: Retrieval needs a gap
statement: Make retrieval ask for something taught earlier after a gap, with it hidden, because a check straight after teaching shows only that the student was following.
detail: A BrainLift on intro videos for a reading course separates retrieval from re-exposure. A question asked before the video about an earlier lesson is real retrieval, because the child has to produce the answer across a gap of days, while the sync check after a video comes too soon after the teaching and checks attention, not memory. It rests the rule on retrieval and spacing research: retrieving strengthens retention more than re-reading (Roediger and Karpicke 2006), and knowledge revisited across spaced intervals is retained far better than knowledge massed (Cepeda et al. 2006). For example, ask for a lesson's key idea from memory at the start of the next part and again later in the unit, instead of restating it.
against: none found; the design rates its basis well evidenced but quotes no studies or effect sizes (the same file, line 172). Matching by text misses a reworded recall: "a reworded recall is not recognised, so check `CLOSE-RECUR-MISSING` by eye before reporting it." (`shadow/content-eval/SKILL.md`, line 201), and recurrence can't be checked when the later lessons are missing (`shadow/content-eval/reports/G3-U2-L1-review.md`, line 229).
